title: Work, Energy and Power
seo_title: Work, Energy and Power Class 11 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 5)

key_big: W = Fd cos θ; W(net) = ΔK.
key_sub: Momentum is conserved in all collisions; KE only in elastic ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

Work W = Fd cos θ is zero when the force is perpendicular to the motion. The work–energy theorem says the net work equals the change in kinetic energy ½mv². Potential energy is mgh near the Earth and ½kx² for a spring. Without friction, mechanical energy is conserved.

Power is the rate of doing work, P = W/t = Fv (1 hp = 746 W). In every collision momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions. Equal masses in an elastic head-on collision exchange velocities.

Example

k = 200 N/m, x = 0.1 m. Energy stored?

½ × 200 × 0.01

Answer: 1 J

Example

F = 1000 N at 20 m/s. Power?

P = Fv

Answer: 20,000 W

Common mistakes

  • Using Fd when the force is at an angle.
  • Thinking kinetic energy is conserved in all collisions.
  • Doubling KE when speed doubles (it becomes four times).
